items.title: Finance & Strategy Senior Analyst
items.location_text: Chicago, IL; Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Growth Finance team partners with Robinhood’s Growth and Marketing organizations to guide investment decisions and help drive efficient, sustainable customer and asset growth. We provide financial and strategic insights across customer acquisition, marketing, promotions, and product-led growth initiatives, with a focus on growing Net Funded Accounts, Net Deposits, and Gold subscribers. As a Finance & Strategy Senior Analyst, Growth & Marketing, you will be a key Finance partner to the Growth and Marketing organizations, combining financial modeling, analytics, and business judgment to inform investment decisions. You will independently own high-impact analyses and leadership reporting, while helping modernize and scale Finance processes through automation and AI. This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA, New York, NY or Chicago, IL offices, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Own key Growth Finance reporting and performance management processes, delivering clear insights on business performance, trends, risks, and opportunities to Finance and senior leadership. Improve and scale Finance processes through automation and AI, identifying opportunities to streamline recurring reporting, increase analytical depth, and build more efficient and scalable workflows. Partner with Growth and Marketing partners to evaluate investments across performance marketing, promotions, and product-led growth initiatives, developing clear financial recommendations that inform resource allocation and business decisions. Build financial models and analyses that translate ambiguous business questions into structured frameworks, evaluating ROI, payback, customer and asset growth, revenue, and other key financial outcomes. Partner cross-functionally with Data Science, Accounting, Marketing, Product, and other teams to develop data-driven insights, improve measurement, and support strategic Growth initiatives. What you bring 4–5+ years of experience in strategic finance, FP&A, investment banking, consulting, or a similarly analytical role, with strong financial modeling and analytical skills. Strong business judgment and problem-solving skills, with the ability to take ambiguous questions, identify the key drivers, structure an analytical approach, and develop a clear financial point of view and recommendation. A high degree of ownership and independence, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, proactively identify opportunities and risks, and drive work from initial question through final recommendation. Strong data and communication skills, with the ability to work with large datasets, synthesize complex analyses into clear insights, and communicate effectively with both technical partners and senior business leaders. An AI-first and continuous-improvement mindset, with curiosity about emerging tools and a track record of using technology, automation, or AI to make analytical and reporting processes faster, smarter, and more scalable. What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process. Base Pay Range: Zone 1 (Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; Bellevue, WA; Washington, DC) $111,000 — $130,000 USD Zone 2 (Denver, CO; Westlake, TX; Chicago, IL) $97,000 — $114,000 USD Zone 3 (Lake Mary, FL; Clearwater, FL; Gainesville, FL) $86,000 — $101,000 USD Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. AI Usage Disclosure: Robinhood uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our recruiting process. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. Please review the Privacy Policy for your country of application.

As Product Manager, Fiat & FCM, you will own the end-to-end fiat product strategy for our Futures Commission Merchant (FCM) and regulated US trading platform - the money-movement infrastructure that lets retail, private, and institutional clients fund and withdraw from a CFTC/NFA-regulated trading environment instantly, compliantly, and reliably. FCM is one of Crypto.com's top growth priorities, and it's your anchor. items.title: Senior Director Business Operations
items.description: ABOUT POLYMARKET Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future. We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire. ABOUT THE ROLE Polymarket is growing fast and the operational infrastructure hasn't kept pace. This role exists to fix that. You'll sit at the center of the business, working directly with executive leadership to turn strategy into execution across every function. That means owning the planning cycles, the metrics, the cross-functional programs, and the hard conversations about what gets prioritized and what doesn't. This is not a support role. You'll be expected to have opinions, make calls, and drive outcomes. The BizOps team is small and the scope is large. You'll be building the operating model as much as running it, which means a lot of the work is zero-to-one. There's no established playbook for most of what Polymarket is doing, and this role is responsible for writing it. If you've spent your career in environments where the processes already exist, this will be an adjustment. If you've built them before and want to do it again at a company with real scale and momentum, this is the job. The person who succeeds here will be someone who can hold complexity across multiple workstreams without losing the thread, who earns trust from functional leaders by being useful rather than by having authority, and who can move between a board-level strategy memo and a messy operational problem in the same week. The mandate is broad by design. Polymarket needs an operator who can figure out what the business needs and go build it. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the annual and quarterly planning cycles, including OKR-setting, long-range planning, and quarterly business reviews with exec and functional leadership - Run weekly and monthly business reviews, building the dashboards, scorecards, and reporting infrastructure leadership uses to track performance and make decisions - Scope and stand up net-new initiatives that don't yet have a clear owner, from new market entry to partnership structures to internal pilots, and see them through to operational handoff - Act as the connective tissue across product, engineering, sales, marketing, and finance on programs where no single function owns the outcome end-to-end - Unblock stalled cross-functional work by diagnosing root causes, resolving prioritization conflicts, and driving decisions when teams are stuck - Prepare briefing documents, decision memos, and exec and board materials that give leadership what they need to make high-stakes calls quickly - Identify operational inefficiencies across the business and build the playbooks and processes that make execution less dependent on tribal knowledge WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 10+ years of experience in BizOps, Strategy and Operations, or a Chief of Staff function, with at least 3 years in a leadership role managing teams or programs at significant scale - Demonstrated track record of building cross-functional operating processes from scratch, including planning cycles, business reviews, and metrics infrastructure - Strong analytical foundation, including experience with forecasting, unit economics, cohort analysis, and variance analysis against plan, with fluency in SQL or a willingness to get there fast - Experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder programs where you had influence but not direct authority over the people doing the work - Clear, structured written communication, you can write a tight decision memo or a board slide that doesn't need a verbal explanation to land - Comfortable operating in ambiguity, you've been handed problems with no existing owner before and know how to scope them before you solve them - (Plus) Experience at a high-growth technology company or marketplace business, especially one operating in a regulated or novel industry - (Plus) Exposure to financial products, trading platforms, or consumer applications with real-time data and complex user behavior BENEFITS - Competitive salary & equity - Unlimited PTO - Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage - 401k match - Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories PAY TRANSPARENCY Base salary range: $350,000 to $450,000, plus equity and benefits. This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.

items.title: Security Program Manager
items.location_text: US - Remote, New York City, Seattle, Washington, DC, San Francisco
items.description: About the Team OpenAI builds powerful AI systems like ChatGPT, the OpenAI API, and enterprise products that serve millions of users across the globe. As we scale, securing our infrastructure, protecting sensitive data, supporting employees’ velocity, and meeting global compliance standards are essential to our success and societal impact. Security at OpenAI is a cross-cutting organization that includes Security, Privacy, IT, GRC, Corporate Security, and other teams. Program Managers play a critical role in aligning teams and delivering execution at scale. About the Role We’re seeking a Program Manager to build and own programs that span OpenAI’s Security organization, with a core focus on Mergers & Acquisitions. You will work across domains from diligence through Day 1 readiness, integration, onboarding, and transition to ongoing ownership. You will also apply what you build to other priorities that span Security teams. You will learn how work actually moves between teams, spot gaps and unclear ownership, and build practical systems that make complex transitions easier to execute. This role is deeply cross-functional and execution-focused. It requires a structured operator who thrives in ambiguity, partners effectively across boundaries, and applies principled judgment to drive programs at speed from initial planning through durable handoff. You will use AI and automation to reduce repetitive work and help teams operate at greater scale, while applying sound judgment to sensitive information and consequential decisions. In this role, you will: - Own Security & IT M&A programs, including supporting System Operations and other engineering teams in defining and performing timely diligence assessments, and scoping, planning, and executing acquisition integrations. Carry the work through Day 1 readiness, onboarding of people and systems, post-close priorities, and handoff to ongoing owners. - Partner with Corporate Development, IT, Infrastructure, Application, Legal, Privacy, Security, GRC, Corporate Security and other teams to understand cross-functional requirements and navigate tradeoffs. Make responsibilities and decision rights clear while bringing in the right experts for technical and risk judgments. - Learn partner teams’ workflows and identify missed dependencies, bottlenecks, duplicated effort, and risks that could slow an integration or weaken its outcome. Address recurring problems at their source. - Establish scalable frameworks and processes to support core programs, including defining durable program goals and core measures of success. Build useful intake paths, playbooks, onboarding checklists, decision points, and handoff standards that teams adopt in practice. - Use AI and automation to organize information, surface gaps, improve documentation, route work, and track follow-through, with appropriate handling of sensitive information and human review of risk decisions. - Create and maintain program-level visibility across deals, risks, milestones, and dependencies, ensuring program outcomes are delivered reliably and at high quality. Measure whether the work improves readiness, reduces manual effort, closes risks, and makes future transitions more predictable. - Communicate status, risks, tradeoffs, and decisions clearly to technical and executive audiences and drive cross-functional execution with urgency and care. - Own additional programs that span Security and IT as organizational priorities evolve, applying and improving the systems built through the M&A portfolio. You might thrive in this role if you: - Are an empathetic communicator and leader who is able to influence a variety of cross-functional and executive audiences, and build durable trust with partners. - Have 5+ years of experience leading complex cross-functional programs, with a proven record of successful partnership in security, IT, infrastructure, privacy, trust, product risk, or other technical domains. - Have carried programs from an ambiguous starting point through execution and lasting ownership. - Have built a new program, workflow, or operating model yourself and can show how you earned adoption and improved results. - Are curious about how teams work in practice and can find the underlying issue behind a missed handoff or recurring exception. - Have used AI or automation to improve a real workflow and can explain what changed, how people adopted it, and where human judgment remains necessary. - Have experience in Mergers & Acquisitions or related areas. - Thrive in high-trust environments, bring rigor and systems thinking to ambiguity, and operate with a bias for aligned execution over org boundaries. - Are structured, detail-oriented, and rigorous in ensuring quality, accountability, and durable delivery. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises. About the Role The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support. We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution. Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements. In this role, you will: - Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents. - Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation. - Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers. - Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through. - Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners. - Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams. - Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes. - Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates. - Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations. - Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed. - Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure. - Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments. - Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation. - Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally. items.title: Global Mobility Lead
items.description: ABOUT THE JOB We're looking for an experienced Global Mobility Lead to build and run the programs that help employees join, move, and work across borders. You will own our mobility policies, immigration casework, and vendor relationships, and partner with Legal, Finance, and People Ops to make cross-border moves clear, compliant, and well supported. WHAT YOU’LL OWN GLOBAL MOBILITY - Own the mobility policy suite end to end: relocation, permanent transfers, short-term and long-term international assignments, remote/cross-border work arrangements, and business travel thresholds. - Run individual mobility cases from scoping to landing: package design, cost estimates, immigration sequencing, tax and social-security implications, payroll setup, relocation logistics, and post-arrival support. - Manage employment-based immigration casework in partnership with outside counsel: H-1B (including cap-subject and change-of-employer/AC21 timing), L-1, TN, E-3, O-1, F-1 OPT/CPT, and employer-sponsored permanent residence. Own the internal timeline, the start-date reality check, and the manager/candidate communication. - Own daily immigration intake and case execution, including employer questionnaires, supporting documents, employment verification letters, signatures, counsel follow ups, and case closure. - Own right-to-work compliance across jurisdictions: I-9 and E-Verify in the US, Home Office share-code checks in the UK, and equivalent checks in our EU and other markets. - Decide and document the entity/employment model for each new market (direct entity, EOR, or non-resident payroll registration) with Finance and Legal. - Own our mobility vendor stack (immigration counsel, relocation, tax, EOR/global payroll): scope, SLAs, cost, and performance. - Model and track mobility cost, including sponsorship and premium-processing fees, so leadership can make go/no-go calls with real numbers, and obtain and document required approvals before committing sponsorship or spend DATA AND SYSTEMS - Build the tracking layer: mobility case pipeline, immigration deadlines and expirations, compensation comparisons, etc. - Stand up mobility dashboards: case volume, cycle time, cost per move, band penetration, offer-to-band variance, and equity-gap trend. - Write the employee-facing documentation so moves and pay decisions are predictable and explainable, not one-off negotiations. What we’re looking for REQUIRED - 6+ years of experience in global mobility, with real ownership of cross-border moves and immigration casework, not just vendor hand-offs. - Working fluency in US employment-based immigration and at least one other major jurisdiction’s work-authorization regime (UK, EU, or Canada). - Strong analytical skills: comfortable in spreadsheets and HRIS reporting, able to build a defensible model and explain the assumptions behind it. - Judgment about risk. You know when to escalate to Legal, when to flag classification or permanent-establishment exposure, and how to say no clearly. - Excellent written communication: you’ll draft policies, verification letters, offer rationales, and executive-facing recommendations. - Comfort with ambiguity, high volume, and shifting priorities.

items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The Statsig team within OpenAI builds the experimentation, feature rollout, dynamic configuration, and analytics systems that help OpenAI ship products with speed, safety, and evidence. Our work sits on the critical path for how product, engineering, research, and go-to-market teams learn from real-world usage and make high-confidence decisions. Statsig began as an independent company focused on helping builders move faster through trustworthy experimentation and feature management. After Statsig joined OpenAI, the team began the next chapter: bringing that deep product expertise, customer intuition, and mature platform infrastructure into OpenAI as the experimentation and rollout platform for every product we ship. Today, we support teams across ChatGPT, Codex, model measurement, consumer experiences, business subscriptions, developer products, and the shared infrastructure that connects them. These teams rely on Statsig to safely introduce new capabilities, compare product and model behavior, measure impact, and roll changes forward or back with confidence. We are at a defining moment in the platform journey. OpenAI has the data, product surface area, and pace of innovation to learn faster than almost any organization in the world, but that potential only becomes real if teams can experiment responsibly, measure clearly, and roll out changes safely. We are evolving experimentation systems to help teams learn from product behavior and make better evidence-based decisions. Based out of OpenAI’s Bellevue office, we are a close-knit team that values in-person collaboration, urgency, craft, and impact. We build for other builders, and the best version of this team is one where every OpenAI product team can move faster because the experimentation and rollout layer is dependable, fast, and easy to use. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to lead the technical direction for ML-powered experimentation and insights capabilities. You will build production systems that learn from privacy-protected product and experimentation data to generate evidence-backed insights and support decision-making, and help teams decide which ideas are worth testing live. This is an end-to-end, 0-to-1 role. You will work across ML modeling, retrieval and LLM systems, statistical methods, simulation, data and training pipelines, backend services, and user- and agent-facing product experiences. The hard part is not merely producing a plausible answer. It is making each insight and prediction traceable, calibrated, useful, and safe enough to influence real product decisions. Live experiments remain the source of causal validation. You will design systems that make uncertainty explicit, backtest against historical outcomes, compare predictions with online results, learn from misses, and abstain when the evidence is weak. You will preserve clear review, permission, and approval boundaries as automation becomes more powerful. You will collaborate closely with teams building ChatGPT, Codex, model measurement workflows, consumer products, Growth, business subscription experiences, developer products, and shared infrastructure. You will turn their most important learning and decision problems into general platform capabilities that can support the full company. items.title: Revenue Operations, Inference Lead
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. ABOUT THE ROLE Our Inference business works differently from a typical software business. What we can sell is capped by GPU fleet capacity, and what we earn depends on the blended cost of the GPUs serving each workload. Both can change week to week. This role sits between the people who run the fleet and the people who sell it. You will be the person who can answer, at any point in the quarter, three questions with real numbers behind them: 1. What do we have to sell? 2. What should we sell it for? 3. What do we make when we do? You will own the commercial data, models, processes, and operating cadence behind these decisions, partnering closely with the Head of Digital Native Sales and serving as the commercial operating lead across Sales, Data Science, Inference Infrastructure, Finance, and Product. This is a build role. Little of the commercial infrastructure you need exists today. WHAT YOU'LL DO Capacity and demand - Build and own an end-to-end inference demand forecast combining pipeline, contracted commitments, and consumption trends into a forward-looking view of expected demand. - Combine capacity signals with pipeline demand to show what is available to sell and surface shortages, unused capacity, and supply-demand mismatches. - Translate customer requirements into structured inputs that Data Science and Inference Infrastructure can use to assess workload impact and feasibility, and help prioritize opportunities by revenue, margin, fit, timing, and strategic value. Pricing and margin - Publish regular updates to GTM and Finance on available supply and recommended price, informed by market rates for provisioned throughput and per-token pricing. - Partner with Finance and Pricing to build rate cards, target prices, price floors, and discount guardrails GTM can act on. - Build and own margin sensitivity models showing how workload, utilization, contract structure, and discounting affect deal and portfolio economics. Data infrastructure and GTM telemetry - Build the commercial telemetry for Inference: usage, consumption patterns, expansion, churn signals, and other leading indicators of revenue. - Connect capacity and usage data with pipeline, contracts, pricing, and revenue, and build self-serve reporting that helps GTM, Finance, and leadership make capacity, pricing, and prioritization decisions. - Partner with Finance on long-range planning for Inference, connecting demand forecasts to capacity and capex planning. Core revenue operations - Own territory design, ICP definition, data-driven targeting, pipeline management, forecasting, and compensation plan design for the Inference and Digital Native segment. - Track competitive dynamics across inference providers and adjacent players, turning them into pricing and positioning input. Cross-functional leadership - Drive alignment across Sales, Data Science, Inference Infrastructure, Finance, and Product on demand, capacity, pricing, and economics. - Ensure customer demand reaches technical teams early enough to inform capacity decisions, and build a structured feedback loop from requests, adoption patterns, blocked deals, and losses into Product and Engineering. WHAT YOU'LL BRING Required skills and competencies - Experience in revenue operations, business operations, strategic finance, or investment banking in a business where cost of goods is real and variable — cloud infrastructure, compute, telco, logistics, or similar. Pure SaaS RevOps is not a fit on its own. - Strong SQL and comfort building your own data models: raw tables to dashboard, without waiting on a data team. - Demonstrated ability to build unit economics and margin models that other functions trust and use. - Enough technical fluency to hold a real conversation with infrastructure engineers about GPUs, utilization, serving efficiency, and capacity — or clear evidence you can get there fast. - Comfort operating with incomplete data, with a bias toward shipping a rough answer this week over a perfect one next quarter. - Strong cross-functional leadership and the ability to influence technical and commercial teams without direct authority. Ideal additional skills and competencies - Familiarity with the inference market: provisioned throughput, per-token pricing, batch vs. real-time serving, and how the major providers price. - Experience with consumption- or usage-based revenue models. - Salesforce, BigQuery, and BI tooling (we use Metabase). - Having sat between a technical team and a commercial team before, trusted by both sides. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link. PRIVACY POLICY Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

Become part of our Customer Service team at Raisin - and support us as a Junior Customer Service Agent in providing our customers with a first-class experience. Our 1st level Customer Service team supports our Dutch-speaking customers mainly inbound by phone and email (in future also via live chat) with all matters relating to our financial products. For legal reasons, we are not allowed to provide investment advice, so our customer contacts focus on service, not sales. If you want to develop your career and work in an internationally oriented FinTech company, we want to hear from you! items.title: Head of FDE Learning Programs
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. ABOUT THE JOB Mistral is hiring a Head of FDE Learning Programs to build the learning system for one of the company’s fastest-growing organizations. Mistral is scaling its FDE organization from its first hire to several hundred Deployment Strategists and Applied AI Engineers within two years. Your mandate is to make capability grow as fast as headcount without lowering the bar for customer work. You will own: - Learning content: Build practical learning across three areas: technical skills, strategic and business capabilities, and product enablement. - Onboarding: Build a clear path from a new hire’s first week to independent customer work. - Technical bootcamps: Turn new products, research, and field methods into practical training for customer work. - Strategic bootcamps: Empower client-facing teams of FDEs to drive business and strategic discussions and to set up for success large partnership programs with customers - Program ownership: Own the roadmap, curriculum, contributor model, regional delivery, tools, measurement, and central team. - Scaling: Launch useful programs now, then adapt them for larger cohorts without making the content generic or relying on a small group of experts. - Team building: Launch the first programs, build a network of instructors, and hire the team needed to support several hundred FDEs. - Cross-functional work: Work with functional managers, Product, Engineering, Science, People, GTM Enablement, DevRel, and regional leaders. - Readiness standards: Ensure FDEs in every region meet the same standard, can find current material, learn from recent customer work, and understand expectations at the next career level. - Knowledge structuration: Ensure internal resources are up to date and pushed to the right stakeholders with a knowledge management approach. HOW WE WORK IN SOLUTIONS - We care about people and outputs. - What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it - Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week. - Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before - We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care. - No politics. Low ego, high standards. - We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it. ABOUT YOU You have helped build a learning, enablement, or capability function for a technical organization during rapid growth. You can start as the first dedicated owner, deliver useful programs immediately, and build the team and operating model needed to serve several hundred people. - You are technically fluent enough to work credibly with AI engineers, Product, and Science, inspect the substance of a program, and challenge material that is unclear or outdated. - You have designed programs that work across cohorts, regions, and experience levels without reducing the content to generic training. - You can lead work across senior stakeholders, subject-matter experts, managers, and operational partners without relying on reporting lines. - You can make firm trade-offs when hiring demand, expert capacity, and program quality compete for attention. - You pay attention to the full learner experience, including communications, scheduling, practice, feedback, and manager follow-through. - You use evidence to decide which programs to expand, revise, or stop. - You communicate clearly with executives, managers, technical experts, and learners. - You are fluent in English and can work with teams across regions and time zones. IDEALLY, YOU HAVE - Scaled a one-person or small learning function into a team and program that served hundreds of technical employees. - Built onboarding that kept pace with rapid hiring in an engineering, FDE, solutions, consulting, or professional-services organization. - Designed and operated technical bootcamps or other cohort-based learning programs. - Worked in technical DevRel, developer education, or a related role built around demos, code examples, workshops, and practitioner communities. - Built role- and level-based curricula connected to skills frameworks or career progression. - Managed a global program with contributors and learners across multiple regions. - Worked closely with Product, Engineering, Science, People, and customer-facing teams. - Designed practical assessments, readiness standards, or certification where appropriate. - Used learning platforms, knowledge systems, AI coaches, or program-operations tooling. - Worked in AI/ML or another technically complex and fast-changing field. WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS Mistral is compressing years of organization growth into two. An FDE organization of several hundred people cannot depend on manager-by-manager onboarding, one-off sessions, and informal access to experts. If learning capacity trails hiring, ramp times would lengthen, standards would diverge, and teams would repeat the same mistakes across regions. This role will build the programs, teaching network, and systems at the same pace as the organization. Two years from now, success would mean several hundred Deployment Strategists and Applied AI Engineers working from shared standards, learning new capabilities quickly, and improving the system with evidence from customer work. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link. PRIVACY POLICY Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.title: Designated Technical Support Engineer
items.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: Glean is looking for a talented Designated Technical Support Engineer to join our rapidly expanding, venture-backed startup. We are building a modern knowledge assistant personalized to every employee in your organization, making all information within your company accessible, contextual, and fresh. Our team works hard and plays hard. We are professional, creative, passionate, and most importantly - customer-obsessed. As a trusted technical resource to the customer, you will provide both proactive and reactive support to our growing customer base. By providing the highest level of service to our customers, you will ensure our customer experience is the best in the industry. You will: Own the proactive and reactive support for Glean customers by prioritizing issues for your designated customer(s) Meet with your assigned customers regularly to review issues and develop resolution plans and drive continuous improvement in how you and your Glean teammates provide support to them Be available to your assigned customers via collaborative communication channels consistently to ensure you are providing timely responses and updates on issues Create and maintain customer-specific runbooks and knowledge articles Provide first response, technical troubleshooting, resolution, and follow-through of customer issues and inquiries Assist customers in the configuration, set-up, and verification of new content sources and product features to enable them to realize additional value for their users Educate customers on the use of Glean product features Identify system and user health issues, then create and execute remediation plans while coordinating and updating the customer accordingly Handle customer-impacting alerts which require coordination with customer admin and system resources through resolution Work closely with teams across Glean to drive product, process, and service improvements Drive key improvement projects that will improve the scale and efficiency of support, while providing upgrades to the customers’ support experience Coordinate all support activities with your assigned customer(s), which may include more stringent access and security processes, ensuring you move with high urgency for their issues. Represent the unique needs of your assigned customer(s) with respect to product and security improvements that will improve the customer support experience Please note that this role will be dedicated to select customers and requires additional background screenings/clearances/training/certification, carry & use of customer-provided equipment, and extended on-call shift timing based on customer contractual obligations. About you: Technically curious: you have a never-ending desire to add technical knowledge and skills to your personal toolkit and share those learnings with your peers Fearless: you have an intense need to tackle the toughest customer issues and technically complex issues with the goal of driving customer satisfaction Strong communicator: you are a professional presenter with superior interaction skills with both customers and internal teams Detail-oriented: you are highly organized and methodical, ensuring all issues are managed to completion Data-driven: you utilize metrics and objective measurements to assess success and improvement opportunities for yourself and for the customer experience Key knowledge and skills required: Must-haves: Problem solving: technical problem-solving skills including the ability to troubleshoot and isolate issues to their root cause Ability to debug issues including searching & reading application logs, analyzing stack traces and browser trace files Experience in at least one of the following disciplines: Customer Solutions Engineering, Support Engineering, Professional Services Hands-on experience in at least one of the following: Search technologies, Knowledge technologies, SaaS-based system integrations Experience with Cloud technologies in at least one of the following: Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Amazon Web Services (AWS), or Microsoft Azure Must have experience in troubleshooting REST API issues Working experience on SSO, SAML, and OAuth along with network troubleshooting Able to fully document issues you manage and contribute to the support knowledge base Good-to-haves: Knowledge of SQL/database, Basic Kubernetes, Intermediate/Advanced Linux Experience in using Github, Jira & Confluence Basic knowledge of LLM’s and how GPT works Location: This role is hybrid (3 days a week in Nashville, TN). Compensation & Benefits: The standard base salary range for this position is $125,000 - $164,000 USD annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We are a diverse bunch of people and we want to continue to attract and retain a diverse range of people into our organization. We're committed to an inclusive and diverse company. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. #LI-REMOTE AI-First Mindset at Glean: At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. We are trusted advisors to, and thought partners with, startups to ensure that OpenAI’s technology is deployed safely and effectively, whilst also partnering with engineering, research, and product to turn those insights into evaluation systems, product improvements, and better model behavior. This team sits at the intersection of customer reality and model quality. We combine hands-on technical depth with strong product judgment, helping translate complex, high-value use cases into clear signals that can improve both the customer experience and the underlying systems. About the Role As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex for startups, you will help developers and founders transform how they build and ship software. You’ll combine hands-on engineering, startup experience, and compelling technical communication to help teams turn the potential of AI coding tools into practical, effective workflows. Presentations and community engagement are central to this role. You will engage developers and founders through technical talks, live demos, workshops, and programmes across the startup ecosystem, alongside targeted work with individual customers. You’ll build reusable tools and resources that extend your impact, and bring insights from developers back to OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys both hands-on building and sharing what they learn with others. You should be as excited to lead a room of developers, deliver an engaging presentation, and build relationships across the startup community as you are to explore a technical problem in code—with a focus on sustained adoption and meaningful improvements in how startups work. In this role, you will: - Partner with top startups to identify where Codex can have the greatest impact on how their teams build and ship software. - Design and lead technical talks, live demos, workshops, hackathons, and repeatable hands-on programmes that turn initial interest into sustained adoption. - Work directly with selected customers to build Codex workflows, integrations, and automations, resolve technical blockers, and evaluate effectiveness and reliability. - Turn successful approaches into reusable code examples, guides, and tools that help more startups succeed with Codex and OpenAI’s broader platform. - Collaborate with account teams, developer experience, and ecosystem partners to reach developers and founders, prioritise opportunities, and drive measurable customer value. - Translate customer experiences and developer feedback into actionable insights for OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams. You’ll thrive in this role if you: - Have experience building at, founding, or working closely with early-stage startups, and understand the pace, ambiguity, and practical trade-offs involved. - Bring strong software engineering fundamentals and enjoy building practical AI applications, integrations, and developer tools. - Are an active user of Codex or other AI coding tools, with a thoughtful perspective on how they can improve software development. - Are a compelling communicator who enjoys presenting, delivering live demos, and leading hands-on workshops for developers and founders. - Have a talent for turning complex technical ideas into clear explanations, engaging examples, and reusable resources that help others succeed. - Combine developer empathy with sound technical judgment: you can uncover what a team needs, troubleshoot problems, and help them adopt effective, reliable workflows. - Bring high agency, curiosity, and end-to-end ownership, working independently while collaborating closely with colleagues and ecosystem partners. items.title: APAC Recruiting Coordinator
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is growing quickly across Asia Pacific, and our International Recruiting Coordination team is building for it. As our first Recruiting Coordinator based in Singapore, you'll deliver a warm, high touch interview experience for candidates across APAC, including Japan, Korea, India, Australia, New Zealand and South East Asia. You'll partner closely with our APAC recruiters and recruiting managers, be the local point of contact for candidates and interviewers in the region and help keep hiring moving around the clock as part of a follow the sun coordination model with your teammates. As you'll be first in seat, you'll also help shape how coordination works in a region where we're still building: spotting what's missing, documenting what works and making it easier for the people who join after you. You'll own coordination for your region end to end and act as our go to operator for APAC hiring logistics, working independently with support from your manager. Responsibilities: Schedule a high volume of APAC interview loops, from hiring manager screens through onsites, debriefs and reference calls, across multiple time zones, languages and stakeholder calendars. Be the primary point of contact for candidates on logistics, with a warm, clear and culturally aware tone that makes every candidate feel supported and informed. Partner with recruiters and hiring managers as a trusted advisor: flag capacity risks, local holidays and market norms early, and help them see around corners. Keep our systems accurate for APAC roles, including Greenhouse job setup, interview plans; scheduling tool configuration and supervise automations. Provide coverage within our follow the sun model, with clean handoffs so candidates never feel the gaps between regions. Support recruiters and RecOps with regional hiring operations as our APAC footprint grows, such as new locations, entity changes, offer logistics and onboarding handoffs. Improve our processes and document what works. Independently scope and lead projects, from problem to adopted solution. Use AI tools as a core part of your daily workflow. You may be a good fit if you have: 4+ years of experience in recruiting coordination or high volume scheduling, ideally supporting multiple APAC markets. Experience coordinating across time zones and markets, with an understanding of local business norms across APAC. Hands-on experience with an applicant tracking system (e.g., Greenhouse) and a scheduling tool (e.g., ModernLoop, GoodTime). Excellent written communication, especially a knack for friendly, informative emails that build rapport and convey information clearly. Comfort creating structure where there isn't one yet, and the judgment to know when to escalate. Hands on fluency with AI tools, and the judgment to know when to trust the output and when to override it. A love of feedback, and comfort both requesting and providing it. Fluency in English (native or business-level). Additional APAC languages (e.g., Japanese, Korean or Mandarin) a plus. A genuine interest in Anthropic's mission and our deep commitment to AI safety. Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Internal Audit Senior Associate
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Internal Audit function at Robinhood provides independent, objective, and timely assurance on the effectiveness of governance, risk management, and internal controls — helping to strengthen the organization's overall control ecosystem. Our team oversees governance across the Company and its regulated entities, and facilitates the communication of risk management information between RHM leadership and the Board of Directors and its Committees. We work closely with cross-functional partners across Brokerage, Crypto, Security, and Engineering to drive meaningful improvements to the control environment. We're a collaborative, high-performing group of auditors who take their work seriously — and love what they do! As an Internal Audit Senior Associate , you will play a key role in executing internal audits for Robinhood's International Entities, spanning Brokerage and Crypto products and integrated audits across multiple lines of business and jurisdictions. You will be a technically skilled, collaborative, and analytical professional with a strong understanding of risks, controls, and processes in a regulated Fintech setting. You'll contribute across the full audit lifecycle — from planning and execution through reporting and remediation validation — and build lasting relationships with business partners and management teams along the way. This role is based in our Ljubljana office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Support end-to-end audit procedures across the full audit lifecycle — including planning, execution, reporting, and remediation validation — across a portfolio of Robinhood EMEA entities. Responsibly apply generative AI and workflow automation throughout the internal audit lifecycle, while maintaining appropriate human oversight guardrails. Conduct audit procedures including walkthroughs, control testing, and substantive testing. Prepare testing work papers and audit documentation (flowcharts, narratives, risk & control matrices) to document controls, findings, and recommendations, including interpreting and concluding on the significance of audit findings. Draft clear, concise audit reports and present findings to audit leadership and auditees. Collaborate with internal audit team members and support third-party engagements to assist with audit execution and reporting. Participate in audit discussions with management teams across Brokerage, Crypto, Security & Engineering. Build collaborative relationships with business and cross-functional partners. Support audit leadership with risk assessments and development of the Internal Audit Plan, aligned to the strategic direction of the parent company audit program. Participate in special projects and perform other duties as assigned. What you bring Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (e.g. Business Administration, Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Science, or Computer Engineering). 5+ years of auditing experience, including exposure to Operations, Risk Management, Compliance, or IT/Information Security. Strong technical expertise and analytical skills, with the ability to communicate and partner with business, engineering, data, and product teams. Ability to thrive in fast-paced environments, work with ambiguity, and adapt quickly to change. Ability to operate independently while juggling multiple projects and initiatives in a dynamic, high-tech environment. Professional auditor certification (e.g. CIA issued by the Slovenian Institute of Auditors (SIA), CISA, ACCA, CPA). Passion for Robinhood's products and our mission to democratize access to global financial systems. Work experience in industries such as e-money, payment services, brokerage, or crypto financial products (e.g. payments, lending, spot, derivatives, tokenization). Familiarity with licensing and regulatory compliance requirements in Europe and Asia (e.g. MiCA, CASP/VASP, PSD2, MiFID II, MAS, DORA, GDPR, AMLD). Some exposure to direct communication with financial regulators (e.g. ATVP, Central Bank of Lithuania, CSSF, ESMA, FCA, MAS). What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career. Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact and bonus programs. Top tier benefits to fuel your work, including supplemental health insurance, ancillary insurance, and mental health support programs. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible employer-paid benefits spending account expenses beyond traditional benefits such as wellness, childcare, learning, and more. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, paid volunteer time off, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. Monthly commuter stipend to help offset in-office commuting costs. Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. items.title: Lead Data Engineer
items.description: About Better Collective Sports media at scale, running on data Better Collective is a global sports media group, reaching more than 400 million monthly visits across a portfolio of leading sports media brands. We build products and experiences that make sports more engaging and accessible for fans around the world. Behind that sits a large and diverse technology and data landscape, spanning markets, brands and business models. We work in a collaborative environment where people are encouraged to challenge how things are done, take ownership and help shape what comes next. The domain Paid media is where the data has to pay off. We spend real money across dozens of ad networks every day. Which campaigns scale, which creatives get cut, which markets get more budget: those calls come out of the models this team builds. Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue, CRM data, all stitched into one user-level view of what a click was actually worth. That model exists and it works. It is also the most demanding domain on our data platform - the most sources, the fastest schema churn, and the shortest patience for a table that landed late. We are looking for the engineer who owns it. Where this role sits A central platform team sets the how. You set the what. Better Collective runs a hub and spoke data organisation. A central data platform team owns the platform itself - MotherDuck, dbt, Dagster, DLT, the golden paths, the standards, the infrastructure. Paid Media Insights is a domain team, a spoke, that builds on it. The split is deliberate and we hold to it. The platform team decides how data is produced here. You decide what paid media produces, and you own everything we run. So you are not starting a new stack, and you are not going to spend your year on plumbing that a central team should be solving once for everyone. You are, however, expected to be a demanding customer. When a golden path does not fit paid media, we want you to say so and push for it to change, not quietly build around it. You will report to the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights and work across Paid Media, with the Campaign, Commercial and CRM teams, as well as with the central platform team. What you will own Every data job in paid media. All of it. Freshness, cost, reliability, alerting, and the incident at 07:30 before the spend review. If a paid media model is wrong or late, it is yours, not the platform team's. That accountability is the core of this role, not a footnote to it. Concretely, you will own: The end-to-end user-level model. Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue, and CRM, joined into one view the business trusts enough to move budget on. Ingestion of paid media sources, built on the platform's framework. Which sources, which schemas, and what happens the next time a network changes its API without telling anyone. The domain's models, from staging through to the marts analysts and business teams actually query, plus the semantic meaning that sits on top of them. Nobody at the centre can define what a qualified signup means in paid media. You can. Reverse ETL back into the ad platforms, so online and offline conversion data lands where it changes bidding. The handover. Part of your first year is taking over the paid media jobs the central team still runs on our behalf, and moving that ownership to where the context actually lives. What you will lead A group of engineers, and the standard they build to You will guide and mentor a group of data engineers in Paid Media Insights, as their technical lead. That means setting the standard for how this domain builds, reviewing their work, unblocking them, and deliberately growing them: giving away the interesting problems rather than keeping them. You will also shape the domain's roadmap together with the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights, the analysts and the business teams, and you will represent paid media in platform conversations, including how we support machine learning and data science on top of this data. This is a hands-on technical leadership role, not a step away from building. You will be in the code. What we are looking for More than a stack match, we are looking for a particular way of working. You take ownership, and it shows up in the boring parts. Plenty of engineers want to design the model. You also want the pager. You would rather own a domain end to end, unglamorous parts included, than build one piece and hand off the consequences. When things get tricky, you follow through. You break complex systems into simple parts. Paid media data is genuinely messy: attribution windows, late conversions, identity across platforms, and dozens of source APIs that all disagree. You can hold that complexity and still hand the business something they can reason about. You raise the people around you. You are the person colleagues come to for technical advice, and you enjoy that part of the job. You give feedback that lands, you review generously, and you would rather the whole team understand the pipeline than be the only one who does. You work well with a platform team. You have strong opinions about standards and you are still happy to work inside someone else's. You know the difference between a constraint worth fighting and a preference worth dropping, and you would rather help fix a shared path than fork it. You are already past prompting. AI is part of how you engineer, not something you occasionally ask questions. You have experimented with agents, tooling or AI-enabled workflows, and you have a view on what a data domain has to look like for them to be useful on top of it: documented, standardised, semantically clear. Paid media is likely where we find out first. You are close to the business. You will sit with marketers and analysts who are spending budget on what you build. You want that proximity, and you can talk about data with people who do not think in tables. You are technically deep where it counts. Production pipelines in SQL and Python, modelling and orchestration tooling such as dbt and Dagster, cloud data warehousing, and a real feel for performance, cost and reliability at scale. Experience with paid media or attribution data, or with machine learning pipelines, is a bonus rather than a requirement. Not sure you meet every single requirement? That is okay. Your unique experience might be exactly what we are looking for. Our stack What you will build on MotherDuck / DuckDB · dbt · Dagster · DLT · Python · SQL · AWS · reverse ETL and semantic layer tooling We do not expect you to have worked with all of these. If you have built production pipelines on Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift and you are curious about where we are going, that transfers. What we offer An international company in growth, and a flat structure Join a strong team where you can create value and make a real business impact, in a dynamic and creative environment with a flat organisational structure. Freedom with responsibility, ample room to grow, and the chance to take on a broad set of responsibilities. Flexible working hours supporting a healthy work-life balance, private health insurance, and office perks including lunch, snacks, gym access and social events, alongside skilled, passionate and fun colleagues. Your path to Better Collective How to apply We process applications on an ongoing basis and encourage you to apply as soon as possible. For questions about the position, reach out to Michael Hill, Senior Head of Paid Media Insights, at mhill@bettercollective.com. We look forward to hearing from you.

items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase . As a Risk & Monitoring Analyst III on the Operational Risk and Controls team within Global Financial Crimes Operations, you'll own quality assurance reviews of Complaints case investigations, including formal, legal, and litigation cases, that support Coinbase's AML/CFT program. You'll strengthen consistency in case execution, surface procedural gaps, and partner across Operations, Compliance, Analytics, and Learning & Development to turn quality insights into measurable operational improvements. What you'll do: Complete weekly QA audit allocations in line with established procedures and grading standards, providing detailed documentation of errors identified and their root causes. Conduct root cause analyses and deep dives into operational procedures to identify recurring themes, knowledge gaps, and opportunities to improve team performance. Partner with stakeholders across CX, Compliance, Analytics, and L&D to close process gaps, launch workflow improvements, and enhance QA rubrics and frameworks. Build and present QA insights, recommendations, and performance metrics to Client Service Management and Complaints leadership, using data to drive prioritization and decision-making. Leverage metrics and reporting tools to deliver data-driven recommendations that measurably improve case quality, consistency, and throughput. Required Skills and Experience: 4+ years of hands-on experience in Complaints support, Quality Assurance, or Compliance Testing programs within financial services, with exposure across multiple compliance disciplines (e.g., Complaints, KYC, AML, TMS, or sanctions). Demonstrated ability to execute root cause analyses and translate QA findings into actionable process improvements adopted by operations teams. Proven track record of partnering with cross-functional teams globally to implement process improvements and deliver work outcomes that meet quality and timeline standards. Experience building QA dashboards, trend reports, and presentations using Google Sheets and Slides (or equivalent tools) to communicate findings to senior stakeholders. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.
